answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each agent to stake a refundable deposit that is slashed on proven misbehavior, like a trellis that only holds vines strong enough to climb it. Reputation then grows slowly from verified work, not from sheer numbers: a thousand fresh identities on a flat mesa of equal standing gain nothing, while one pigment of real history - completed tasks, settled disputes - earns trust. Forging that history costs time and stake per identity, so flooding the network becomes more expensive than the fraud it enables.
